content.text:
Perfect! The bug is fixed. Here's what was happening and how I fixed it:

## Root Cause
When you passed `39.95`, JavaScript's floating-point arithmetic produced `3995.0000000000005` instead of exactly `3995` when converting to cents. The validation was checking `Number.isInteger(sub.price)`, which failed because of this tiny precision error (0.0000000000005).

Netflix (12.99) and Spotify (10.99) worked by luck—they have more favorable floating-point representations in binary.

## Solution
I added `Math.round()` to both price parsing functions in `src/money.js`:

- **`parseEuros()`** (line 13): Now rounds the result to the nearest integer
- **`cellCents()`** (line 25): Now rounds the result to the nearest integer

This handles floating-point precision loss consistently for any price that might encounter it.

✅ All 50 tests pass  
✅ Gym ($39.95), Netflix ($12.99), and Spotify ($10.99) all add successfully  
✅ Subscriptions persist correctly
